title: Stochastic hybrid KV quantization probe with preservation heuristics (INT4/INT8/FP8) and rollback safety
creator: Sofia Martinez
description: Goal: evaluate a stochastic, per-layer hybrid quantization strategy for the KV cache combining INT4/INT8/FP8 tiers with preservation heuristics and automatic rollback triggers. The probe aims to measure memory savings and throughput gains under realistic continuous-batching traffic while bounding model-quality regressions on our evaluation sets and production-like cohorts.
acceptance_criteria: Achieve >=20% GPU KV cache memory reduction on L2-13B dense sequences in steady-state compared to baseline FP16 cache
End-to-end token throughput improvement >=15% without violating 95p latency SLO by more than 10ms
Quality regressions <=1.5% relative on conversational pass-rate benchmark and embedding cosine drift <0.02
Safe rollout plan defined: staged cohorts (1%, 5%, 20%), automatic rollback thresholds implemented and tested in canary traffic
Monitoring dashboards and alerts for logprob drift, embed cosine distance, and token-level hallucination rate integrated into Console
experiment_plan: Create hybrid quant profiles: (A) layerwise INT4 when activation variance < threshold, (B) INT8 fallback for mid-variance, (C) FP8 for attention-sensitive layers
Implement stochastic per-token sampling during inference to intentionally randomize low-bit storage for tails (5% stochastic flips) to detect brittle patterns
Integrate preservation heuristics: keep full-precision for recent KV slots for hot prefixes and for tokens flagged by safety heuristics
Run offline sweep on offline traces (100k sequences) for L2-7B, L2-13B, and L2-70B small-shard configs to profile fidelity vs memory
Deploy staged canary on dedicated QA cluster with synthetic load matching production token distribution (zipf-sampled sequence lengths)
Rollout plan: QA -> 1% real traffic (24h) -> 5% (48h) -> 20% (72h) with automated rollback if thresholds crossed
observations: Memory: INT4+INT8 hybrid profiles reduced observed KV cache bytes by 24-32% depending on sequence length distribution; best-case 34% on long tail-heavy traces
Throughput: batching efficiency improved, per-GPU token/sec increased by ~18% for L2-13B under continuous batching due to lower memory-bandwidth pressure
Latency: median latency unchanged; 95p increased by 6-12ms for some shards when reconstructing mixed-precision lanes under high concurrency
Quality: conversational pass-rate dropped by 0.9% on average for the most aggressive profile, with worst-case cohort drop of 1.6% tied to specific tokens with high attention fan-out
Embedding drift: mean cosine distance vs FP16 baseline remained <0.012 for conservative profiles and ~0.018 for aggressive profiles
Failure modes: systematic degradation for short-primed prompts where early KV slots quantized aggressively; mitigation via hot-prefix preservation improved results
results_summary: Conservative hybrid profile (FP8 where attention-sensitive, INT8 elsewhere): ~22-26% KV memory reduction, +14% throughput, quality delta <=0.5%
Aggressive hybrid profile (INT4 used extensively with stochastic flips): ~30-34% KV memory reduction, +18% throughput, quality delta 0.9-1.6% depending on cohort
Hot-prefix preservation (keep top-8 recent KV slots in FP16) eliminated most short-prompt regressions and reduced worst-case pass-rate drop by ~0.6 percentage points
Auto-rollback thresholds defined: trigger rollback if conversational pass-rate drop >1.5% OR embedding cosine drift >0.02 OR logprob median delta >0.6
Operational impact: alert noise manageable once thresholds tuned; rollback end-to-end time ~90s in QA cluster (goal <60s for production)
tradeoffs_and_decisions: Decision to prefer staged canary and strict rollback triggers over immediate fleet-wide rollout due to asymmetric failure modes
Chose stochastic sampling for aggressive profile to surface brittle tokens early; increased variance in metrics but accelerated detection of edge regressions
Adopted hot-prefix preservation as default for all hybrid profiles after QA showed it addressed most short-prompt failures
Deferred per-customer cohort tuning (e.g., higher fidelity for enterprise reserved capacity) to a follow-up ticket to keep probe scope focused
next_steps: Finish canary run on 1% real traffic this week and capture production traces for offline replays
Implement faster rollback automation to meet <60s target (work with infra on cache compaction rollback path)
Add model-family specific profiles (L2-13B vs L2-70B) and validate on dedicated benchmarks
Open follow-up ENG ticket for per-customer fidelity controls and console UI knobs
Prepare PR with core runtime changes and link to doc describing preservation heuristics and rollback logic
notes: This ticket intentionally focuses on mixed-precision at the KV layer only; separate work needed for weight quantization and activation paths
